You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Drawing diagonals could indicate positioning three items at every step along that slope. I definitely need to request a demo for clarity.

I'm checking the layout: starting with r6 full width, which gives me 8s for cols 9-13. I’m thinking that each marker probably serves as the focal point of the design, suggesting a motif structure of 5/2/8. There’s this horizontal base line that connects all the markers together, which could create a cohesive look. It's exciting to explore how this unfolds!

At every marker (r,c), add a motif and its horizontal base: row r-2, cols c-2..c+2 = color 5; row r-1 has color 2 at c-2,c+2 and color 5 at c; row r has color 2 at c-2,c+2 and preserves marker 3 at c; row r+1 has color 2 at c-2,c+2; row r+2 is a full-width color-2 horizontal line, with cols c-2..c+2 changed to color 8. Leave other motif cells at background 0. Preserve all markers. Each marker independently generates one pattern, which must fit in-grid as in the examples. Demo: 16x16 markers at (4,11),(10,3), outputs exactly the described local 5x5 motif plus full-width base rows 6 and 12, where the 5-cell marker-centered patches are 8. Solved test 17x19 markers (3,4),(8,11),(13,6), producing full-width base rows 5,10,15 and 5-centered motifs. Caution: bottom row r+2 is not merely a 5-wide strip: color 2 extends across the whole grid, while color 8 occupies marker-centered width 5. The upper 4 rows do not extend beyond the 5x5 motif. Background is 0, marker color 3, motif colors 5/2/8 in this instance." ); entry
